<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose  
   • Chatterino2 is a native desktop chat client for Twitch.tv, built in C++ with the Qt framework.  
   • It connects to multiple chat-and-event APIs (Twitch IRC, Twitch PubSub/EventSub, third-party emote services such as FFZ/BTTV/SevenTV, pronouns APIs, etc.), parses messages, applies filters/highlights, and renders them in a rich Qt GUI.  

2. Analyze the file structure  
   • Top‐level “src/” houses the application core, controllers, providers, messages, widgets, utilities, singletons, and entry point (main.cpp).  
   • “lib/” contains bundled third-party libraries (websocketpp, sol2, RapidJSON, etc.).  
   • “resources/” has icons, themes, QSS, sound files, license notices.  
   • “controllers/” implement the Model–View–Controller pattern for features: accounts, commands, filters, plugins, notifications, etc.  
   • “providers/” encapsulate external data sources: network APIs (IRC, PubSub, REST).  
   • “common/” and “util/” hold shared types, parsers, helpers, and the network layer (NetworkManager, WebSocketPool).  
   • “widgets/” defines all Qt UI elements—windows, dialogs, views.  
   • “singletons/” expose global services: Settings, Resources, Logging, Updates, CrashHandler.  
   • Build configuration via CMakeLists.txt, CI scripts in “.github/workflows”, and platform installers in “.CI/”.  

3. Examine the README for additional insights  
   • Confirms use of Qt, CMake, multiple platforms (Windows, macOS, Linux, FreeBSD).  
   • Mentions contributions, Doxygen, packaging.  

4. How to draw the system design diagram  
   a. Main components:  
     1. GUI Layer (Qt Widgets & Windows)  
     2. Controller Layer (AccountController, CommandController, FilterController, PluginController, etc.)  
     3. Model Layer (data models for channels, messages, settings, user data)  
     4. Provider Layer (Network providers for Twitch IRC, PubSub, EventSub, FFZ, BTTV, SevenTV, Pronouns, RecentMessages API)  
     5. Core Services / Singletons (Settings, Resources, Logging, CrashHandler, UpdateManager)  
     6. Network Layer (NetworkManager, WebSocketPool, HTTPRequest/Response)  
     7. Data Storage (local settings file, cache directories)  
     8. External Services (Twitch IRC server, Twitch Helix REST API, Twitch PubSub/EventSub websockets, third-party REST endpoints)  
   b. Relationships & interactions:  
     • GUI <--> Controllers (user actions dispatch to controllers)  
     • Controllers <--> Models (update models, emit signals)  
     • Controllers <--> Providers (invoke network calls, subscribe to websockets)  
     • Providers <--> Network Layer (NetworkManager handles HTTP, WebSocketPool multiplexes connections)  
     • Providers <--> External Services (real-time message streams, REST endpoints)  
     • Models <--> GUI (models exposed to Qt views for rendering)  
     • Singletons <--> All components (global config, resource loading, logging)  
   c. Architectural patterns & principles:  
     • MVC / MVVM pattern for GUI parts (widgets bind to models via controllers)  
     • Dependency injection via singletons for cross-cutting concerns  
     • Asynchronous, event-driven I/O (NetworkTask, WebSocket callbacks, Qt signal/slot)  
     • Plugin architecture (Lua scripts loaded by PluginController, sandboxed APIs)  
     • Modular provider pattern (each external API encapsulated in its own namespace)  
   d. Key technologies & libraries:  
     • Qt (GUI, threading, signals/slots, resource system)  
     • websocketpp (WebSocket communication)  
     • RapidJSON (JSON parsing/serialization)  
     • sol2 (Lua integration for plugins)  
     • CMake, vcpkg (build & dependency management)  
     • Boost (some utilities), OpenSSL (secure websockets/HTTPS), miniaudio (sound playback)  

5. Guidelines for tailoring the diagram  
   • For this desktop app:  
     – Use a layered diagram style: place UI at top, services/providers in middle, network layer at bottom, external systems on the far right.  
     – Emphasize real-time flows: IRC messages → WebSocketPool → Provider → Controllers → Models → GUI.  
     – Show asynchronous arrows for network callbacks & Qt signal/slots.  
     – Highlight plugin boundary: PluginController <--> Lua API <--> Plugin scripts.  

6. Diagram elements to include  
   • Clear labels: “Qt GUI”, “CommandController”, “TwitchIRCProvider”, “WebSocketPool”, etc.  
   • Directional arrows:  
     – Solid arrows for control/data flow (e.g., Controller → Provider)  
     – Dashed arrows for event/callback flow (e.g., WebSocket event → Provider → Controller)  
   • Color coding or shapes:  
     – Rectangles for internal modules  
     – Cylinders for data stores (settings file, cache)  
     – Clouds for external systems (Twitch IRC server, REST APIs)  
     – Rounded boxes for singletons/global services  

7. Final pointers  
   • Be exhaustive: include major subsystems (controllers, providers, widgets) but you need not list every single controller.  
   • Capture asynchronous vs. synchronous interactions distinctly.  
   • Group related modules (e.g., all “src/controllers/commands/builtin/twitch” under “Twitch Command Controllers”).  
   • Place build/CI components outside the runtime diagram—these are orthogonal to the architecture.  
   • Use a consistent visual legend for shapes/colors so the reader immediately grasps component types.  
   • Keep the diagram at a level of abstraction that highlights runtime behavior and module boundaries without drowning in file-level detail.  
</explanation>
